## 3. The evidence that moved it
**Zero of June's five nominated checkpoint targets reappear.** Not one of
Siglec-G/10, CMTM4, STS2, Piezo1 or TTLL12 is named anywhere in the month. The
observed half-life of a novel surface checkpoint name in this corpus is under a
month for the genuinely new ones; older validated names resurface to fill the
slot. What July has instead is LILRB4, galectin-9, PILRalpha-CD99, TIM-3, CD30,
HPK1, ICOS and B7-H3 — a fresh list with no members in common with the last one.

**Both CD47 phase 3 readouts are in this month**
([ENHANCE-2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40009500/) and
[ENHANCE-3](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40233321/), *Blood*, 31 July).
Neither title states a direction, which is why neither is carded here: the corpus
knows these programmes ended, but it does not know it *from these rows*, and a
card that recorded the outcome would be recording something the reader inferred.
The direction is settled in the 2026-07 briefing, from a *JCO* phase 3 report
that states it.

**Two simple-baseline results in one month.**
[40662806](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40662806/): deep-learning sequence-based
protein-interaction predictors plateau at 0.65 accuracy under unbiased
evaluation. [40605002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40605002/): plain Z-scores
outperform purpose-built methods for CRISPR paralog synthetic-lethality screens.
With June's two, that is four such results in eight weeks, a full year before the
corpus recorded the pattern as emerging.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[40707132](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40707132/) (*JITC*) is the cleanest
surrogate-versus-endpoint inversion in the corpus, and it is stated in one title:
constitutive IL-7 signalling **promotes CAR-NK survival in the solid tumour
microenvironment but impairs tumour control**. Persistence is the field's
standard proxy for efficacy in engineered cell therapy.

[40668889](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40668889/): perturbing S100A8/A9 — a
canonical MDSC axis and an active drug target — *blunts* antitumour immunity by
promoting protumorigenic myelopoiesis.
[40628269](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40628269/): the costimulatory molecule
ICOS **limits** memory-like properties of exhausted PD-1+ CD8 T cells. ICOS
agonism was in first-in-human trials at the time.
[40624238](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40624238/): IL-17A-secreting
gamma-delta T cells promote resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors — immune-mediated
resistance to a drug class that is not an immunotherapy.

[40645662](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40645662/): shared epitopes create
safety *and efficacy* concerns across several cancer vaccines. Shared-antigen
vaccines are the off-the-shelf alternative to personalization, and this says the
shortcut has its own failure mode.

[40193715](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40193715/) (*Blood*): post-immunotherapy
lineage switch is an emergent form of relapse in leukaemia — the tumour changes
lineage rather than losing the antigen, which no antigen-escape model predicts.

### (b) Method credibility

[40794862](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40794862/) (*NAR*): **errors are
prevalent in lab-made plasmids worldwide.** The most widely shared physical
reagent in molecular biology, audited at scale.

[40682824](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40682824/): untargeted reads in
G4-targeted CUT&Tag enrich at accessible chromatin and restrict identification of
G4-forming sequences — i.e. a body of published G-quadruplex maps may be
accessibility maps. The dispute continues into November with a commentary and a
rebuttal, which is what a live disagreement looks like and is worth more than a
quiet correction.

[40560601](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40560601/): structural gene annotation
choice materially changes orthology inference. Filed with the reference-genome
cards from October and November: the substrate, not the algorithm, is what
decides the answer.
